Officially Saddening: Peugeot Quits WEC, Stellantis' Opel and Citroen Brands Leaving Formula E
7 photos
Photo: Stellantis
Following a Le Figaro report, Stellantis confirmed that it's canning the 9X8 program. The immediate World Endurance Championship exit will be followed by Citroen and Opel pulling out of Formula E after the 2026-27 season, allowing the multinational group created by the merger of PSA and FCA in January 2021 to refocus on customer racing programs and road-going performance models.
Peugeot's departure from endurance racing follows the conclusion of the 2026 season earlier this month. Although the French brand was prepping a revised 9X8 for the 2027 campaign, all that development work has been for nothing . The Citroen and Opel divisions get a little more time in Formula E, for the 2026-27 season finishes in July 2027 with the Tokyo ePrix at the Tokyo Street Circuit.
Looking at the bigger picture, the 9X8 has always been a bit of an unusual proposition. The Lion of Sochaux initially sent its hybrid prototype racer without a rear wing, relying on an outlandish aerodynamic concept that did not work as intended. As such, the 9X8 later gained a rear wing.
All subsequent revisions failed to deliver a competitive breakthrough, and this is part of the reason why the WEC program had to be canned. Four podiums and a lonely pole are the highlights of its five-year campaign, with the works team never winning a race.
Peugeot had a third major upgrade on the menu for the 2027 season, with team principal Emmanuel Esnault promising improvements that would make the 9X8 a regular podium contender. Preps went beyond engineering, with Peugeot already confirming Alex Quinn and Robert Shwartzman for its 2027 driver lineup.
This particularly frustrating development can be explained with numbers. More specifically, the hypercar operation is estimated to cost more than €30 million annually. Stellantis has yet to disclose how much it'll save by leaving the World Endurance Championship.
Photo: Stellantis Although Formula E is losing two Stellantis brands in July 2027, Opel's situation is particularly awkward. Citroen replaced Maserati in the championship, but Opel developed its own Formula E operation around Gen4 regulations. In other words, Opel hadn't even started its Formula E career when the parent company decided that enough is enough.
This, in turn, gives the German outfit a single Formula E season to prove its mettle. Stellantis underlined that its motorsport arm will not be shut down in its entirety. Instead, engineering resources will be moved toward customer racing, with an emphasis on rally cars. Lancia's WRC2 effort comes to mind, a partnership that won the WRC2 teams' championship in 2026.
For some reason, the attached release does not touch upon Lancia Corse HF's 2027 campaign. Be that as it may, its announcement specifically identifies road-going performance models from a total of five brands: Maserati, Alfa Romeo, Lancia, Opel, and Peugeot. Confirmed high-performance monikers include Veloce for Alfa Romeo, GTi for Peugeot , HF for Lancia, and GSE for Opel and its griffin-badged British twin.
Just around 200 people currently working at Stellantis Motorsport will be redeployed into customer racing, performance development, and other activities. Today's decision does not cover Dodge, whose return to the NASCAR Cup Series in 2027 remains unaffected. Stellantis North America, which operates as FCA US LLC, directly funds and manages the American brand's NASCAR return.
Dodge exited the Cup Series after the 2012 season finale in November 2012, right after Brad Keselowski won the championship in his Penske Dodge Charger. Instead of building its own engine, Dodge partnered with Earnhardt Childress Racing to supply a rulebook-compliant V8. The naturally aspirated 5.8-liter V8 is capable of making 800 horsepower on short tracks and road courses.
